headline: San Francisco's Board of Supervisors has voted unanimously for a 45-day pause on approving new data centers, pending the mayor's action.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: a clear local vote that joins a spreading pattern, but it is a short pause that still needs the mayor.
importance_line: Residents in neighbourhoods near planned sites gain time to weigh in and developers face a pause, but the moratorium is not yet in force, lasts only 45 days unless extended, and the city has few data centers.
summary: The San Francisco Standard reports that the city's Board of Supervisors voted unanimously on 6 Oct 2026 for a 45-day moratorium that pauses city approvals of data centers while the Planning Department studies their impacts; it awaits action from Mayor Daniel Lurie and could be extended to 22 months. The Standard notes that Oakley, Richmond and Gilroy already have moratoriums and Oakland and Hayward are considering them.
notes: Read in full. The Standard corrected an early version that said the moratorium took effect immediately; it awaits the mayor.
